author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function finds the **minimum absolute difference** between any two distinct numbers in every **k×k subgrid** of the input grid. It creates a 2D array where each cell contains a **Set** of all unique values from the corresponding k×k window, then sorts each Set and calculates the smallest difference between consecutive elements, handling single-element cases by returning 0.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This solution uses the same approach as Solution 1 — extracting unique values from k×k subgrids into Sets and finding the **minimum difference between consecutive sorted values** — but simplifies the difference calculation logic by always initializing `minDiff` to **Infinity** and then converting it to **0** at the end if no pair differences were found, rather than checking the Set size upfront.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This is a more **memory-efficient variant** that avoids storing Sets in the DP array; instead, it creates a temporary Set for each k×k subgrid, immediately processes it to find the minimum difference, and stores only the final result in the DP cell. It uses a **`continue` statement** to skip processing when a subgrid has only one unique element, leaving that cell at its initialized value of 0.
